result.topic_en: Riemann's calculation for one-dimensional gas flow in Riemann invariants p, q: interchanging dependent and independent variables (hodograph transformation) turns the equations into a linear second-order equation for a potential w(p,q).
result.transcription:
$\log\varrho + \frac{u}{a} = [-2p-] 4p$ \quad $\frac{\partial p}{\partial t} = -(u+a)\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}$ \quad $u = 2a(p-q)$
$\log\varrho - \frac{u}{a} = 4q$ \quad $\frac{\partial q}{\partial t} = -(u-a)\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$ \quad $p = \varphi(x)$ \quad $q = \psi(x)$ \quad $t=0$
$dp = \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}dx + \frac{\partial p}{\partial t}dt$ \quad $\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\frac{\partial q}{\partial t} - \frac{\partial p}{\partial t}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x} = R$
$dq = \frac{\partial q}{\partial x}dx + \frac{\partial q}{\partial t}dt$
$R\,dx = \frac{\partial q}{\partial t}dp - \frac{\partial p}{\partial t}dq$ \quad $[-dx =-] \frac{\partial x}{\partial p} = \frac{\frac{\partial q}{\partial t}}{R}$
$R\,dt = -\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}dp + \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}dq$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial q} = (u+a)\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial p} = (u-a)\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}$ [?] \quad $(x-(u+a)t)\,dp - (x-\overline{u-a}\,t)\,dq = dw$
$2at = \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p\,\partial q} = -\frac{\partial w}{\partial p} - \frac{\partial w}{\partial q}$
$\frac{\partial(x-(u+a)t)}{\partial q} = 2at = -\frac{\partial(x-u-a)t}{\partial q}$ [?]
$\frac{\partial(x-(u-a)t)}{\partial p} = -2at$ \quad $\frac{\partial w}{\partial p} = x-(u+a)t$ \quad $\frac{\partial w}{\partial q} = -(x-\overline{u-a}\,t)$
1) $\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p\,\partial q} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial p} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial q} = 0$
$dp = \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}(dx-(u+a)dt)$
$dq = \frac{\partial q}{\partial x}dx$
[Figure: axes $p$ (horizontal) and $q$ (vertical) with a descending line segment]
$f(p,q)$
